This is a fun exercise, but I struggle to imagine any way that a building automation system could actually kill its occupants. The thing about it is that BAS equipment/system manufacturers don't want any kind of liability for stuff like this, so they are engineered in such a way that it is difficult to actually hurt any people or equipment.

To be more specific, in the case of gas-fired equipment (eg. boiler or furnace, with the goal of creating a CO hazard), BAS systems don't actually go down any further into the equipment than they absolutely have to. They give the equipment a start command (like a thermostat would), and the ignition sequence is controlled by the on-board controller. The BAS system is not able to bypass the flame sensor or air flow switch, so creating an intentional gas leak or combustion gas accumulation is impossible to do without physically going into the equipment and rewiring it.

To the fridge/food poisoning example, I imagine that the fridge would only accept a setpoint signal within certain parameters, so giving it a signal above say 40F would be ignored by the equipment. It would go to its highest allowable setpoint and stop there. If you could get into the fridge's software you might be able to change this, but I doubt the AI would be able to make changes in this way.

And as far as locking the owner in the house, door systems also don't allow this. There is a physical mechanism in them that is independent of the electronically actuated mechanism, so they can always be opened from the inside (for emergency egress).

The best bet is to get the owner to do something that causes him to kill himself or to get someone else to kill him.

TL;DR - Even if it wanted to, a home automation system would be pretty much unable to hurt you in any way.
